judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: [visual context] This is one of the seven "Ver programa" links in the education-programs carousel (#programs-carousel); this one goes to /educativo/programas/acesseparaperceber. In the snapshot all seven carousel slides are in the accessibility tree (no aria-hidden), and each link's name comes only from its contents, "Ver programa", with no title or aria-describedby. It is not inside a paragraph, list item or table cell: it sits beside its description paragraph in a div. The program's title ("Acesse para Perceber") is an SVG logo image with no alt, so it gives assistive technology nothing. The carousel section has no heading of its own, so the nearest heading before all seven links is the same h5, "Arte para Maiores | Daquilo que nos escapa | Encontro online", from the schedule cards. Their context is the same, so by R1 they form one set. The hrefs are seven different program pages (arteparamaiores, monnaescola, euparticipo, primeirospassos, acesseparaperceber, monparatodos, feriasnomon), and the packet's destination headings show different programs, so the resources are not equivalent. A sighted user can tell the links apart by the visible logo title, the photo and the description in each card (screenshot crop), so by R1 elementFails is yes. claimTrue: the count of seven and seven destinations is right, and nothing in the link's programmatic context tells it apart. The paragraph beside it names the program, but it is not the link's paragraph. captureDiffers: I fetched the live server HTML and it has the same seven links, hrefs, alt-less logo images and no heading in the section, so no. The claim names the real failure, so the label is true_positive.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: Row with no claim. The element is the exhibition card link in the "Em cartaz" tab panel, going to /exposicoes/o-verso-da-pagina-contem-o-outro-lado. Its accessible name comes from its contents: the date "Até 28 de março de 2027" and the h3 "O verso da página contém o outro lado". That is the exhibition's title, and it matches the destination's heading, so the link text alone gives its purpose. No other link in the snapshot shares this name. The missing space in the concatenated name ("2027O") does not hide the purpose. The live server HTML still has this card, so captureDiffers is no. The element meets 2.4.4, so a missed failure here would be a false positive.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the newsletter ("Receba notícias") e-mail input. Its placeholder "Seu e-mail" is its only visible label: there is no label element and no other visible text for it. The live CSS sets *::placeholder to var(--chakra-colors-gray-400) = #A0AEC0, the input's background is inherit, and the form panel is white (screenshot crop). I compute 2.26:1 for #A0AEC0 on #FFFFFF, as the claim says, well below 4.5:1 for 18px text at weight 400. Placeholder text is visible text and none of 1.4.3's exceptions applies (it is not an inactive component, decoration, a logo or invisible), more so when it is the field's only label. The live HTML and CSS match the capture, so captureDiffers is no. The element fails 1.4.3 for the reason claimed: true_positive.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the newsletter name input. Its placeholder "Seu nome completo" is its only visible label. The live CSS gives placeholders #A0AEC0 (chakra gray-400) on the input's inherited white background (screenshot crop shows it pale grey on white). That is 2.26:1, which I computed myself, below the 4.5:1 that 18px text at weight 400 needs. Placeholder text is text, and no 1.4.3 exception covers it, especially when it is the only label. The live page matches the capture, so captureDiffers is no. It fails 1.4.3 as claimed: true_positive.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the text input with placeholder "Seu nome completo" in the "Receba notícias" newsletter form. It collects the user's own full name, which is the "name" input purpose in WCAG 2.1 section 7. The captured HTML and the live server HTML both have no autocomplete attribute (and no name attribute), and nothing else exposes the purpose programmatically, so H98 is not met and the purpose cannot be programmatically determined. captureDiffers: the live input is identical to the snapshot. It fails 1.3.5 for the reason claimed: true_positive.
